Did you work that Sunday? No, sir. I had that weekend off. We wound up going to my mother- in-law's. I had to put some safety rails up for her because she just had her knee surgery done and I was putting rails up for around a porch and a bathroom and a tub and everything so she can have something to grab on when she was moving. Okay. And who went out to Lumberton that weekend with you? That was me, my wife, my son and my two granddaughters. Yeah. I'm sorry. I started using their names. Yes, sir. Would you return to work or supposed to return to work that Monday then? So, when you would have to be out at the farm at 5:30 in the morning, I usually got up around about 4:00 in the morning so I could get up, get my coffee in me, and I would read my Bible something there too. Just get a good day started. And then I'd go to work. I would listen to my preaching on work and I sit out there and got dressed, took a shower, and then I'd go up there. I had what they call a daily book. If you've ever been to Christian, you know what I'm talking about? They got their prescription in there for different days. So, let me ask you then, if you had to get up at, I don't know, 3:00 or 4:00 in the morning- ... what time would you go to bed the previous night? About seven, seven, eight, give or take. All right. So, now I'm going to go to November 12th, that Sunday. Y'all were back from Lumberton. You know you have to go to work on the 13th, that Monday. About the same, but you know what I mean? Around 4:35. Okay. Then on the night of the 12th, who all was at the house at the night of the 12th? All right. And at some point, what time do you go to bed? Then when you go to bed, is David there or is he somewhere else or do you know? And when you say his friends, do you know their names? I know Jamie and Andrew. Oh, a guy named Michael, I think is what his name is, and a few other kids that I didn't know. I used to let them hang out in my house and have a bonfire. That way I know they were safe. All right. So you go to bed, David's outside, Savannah, Paitin and Lisa are inside when you go to bed? And that's normal, you normally sleep at night in your bedroom? Yes, sir. Usually I go in there and lay down. Usually the grand babies that come in there and lay with me. And I don't know something, I can put one of them to sleep. If they don't want me to go to sleep, they get in there with papa. I start rocking, singing a little bit and they say ... I know they're asleep. Lisa come and pick one up, take her to bed and bring the other one in and I knock her out. Lisa takes her to bed. All right. So you go to bed between 8:00 or 9:00 that night. Then at some point you wake up early morning hours of November 13th. All right. At some point, did Savannah ever come into your room? Yes, sir. I think I was falling back asleep and she came in there and told me that the baby was acting silly, that Paitin was acting silly, and I thought they were just in there playing. And I told her to go back to bed. I have no idea 'cause I wasn't looking at my clock or nothing else. It was dark. Well, let's stop. Just let me ask the questions and you answer the questions. So you tell her, she comes in there and says, "Something's wrong with Paitin." Yes, sir. "She's acting silly," I think, it was what she was saying, crazy or silly. I can't remember the exact words, sir. And you said, "Go on back in there and go to sleep." And at some point, do you go all the way back to sleep or do you- About time to get up and she goes in there to make my cup of coffee, make her coffee so I can get up and start going. I went in there and she was holding the baby and she said, "Baby, something ain't wrong. Ain't something right wrong. Ain't something wrong." Said, "Call 911." You know what I mean? I couldn't, but I trust my wife's instinct and I knew something was wrong. Sir, that's when I said, "Let's call 911." And then I went in there and started getting dressed. David came out, we got dressed and 911 didn't answer. So that's when we came up with the idea, let's jump in the car and get there. 'Cause by the time the ambulance gets to Pender County and come back, you know what I mean? I could already be at Pender County. Boo Boo. Who's that? I mean, that's his nickname. I'm sorry. I've been calling him since he was a kid. David. All right. And David has Paitin and where does he get into? All right. You've heard Lisa here testify it took about- You're saying it took you about four or five minutes? Yes, sir. You can ask Leatherwood because Leatherwood timed it. He asked me how did I get there so quick from a 911 call until they actually seen David there. And I asked him, "Could I go to jail if I tell them?" He told me no. And I said I averaged out about 120, topped out at 160. Were you able to see while you were driving what Paitin looked like at that Time? I kept my eye on the road going that fast, but I could smell when she defecated and that's when I really punched it. I couldn't tell you. Like I said, my eyes were on the road. You end up getting to Pender County Memorial to the ER? My son got out, banged on the door, and while he was banging on the door, I took my car 'cause I didn't want my car to be right there where the ambulance comes in at, and I took my car and I parked it around in the parking lot and I came through the front door. All right. At some point, was Paitin transferred to New Hanover County? All right. And did you travel down to New Hanover County? I went down 117 and then hit Castle Hayne Road that way and went 'cause it's the fastest way to go. Did anybody ride with you down to the New Hanover Hospital? She was in our van taking Savannah and everything down there. I don't know if she took my mom with her or not, 'cause my mom came out there at Pender County too. All right. And you at some point get down to New Hanover Hospital? Do you get to see Paitin at the hospital when she was in New Hanover? I got to see her when they was bringing her out the, what you call it, and act like they didn't want me to touch her or do nothing with her and I didn't know what was going on. I'm going, "Why not?" And that's when the security guard said, "You got to wait till a cop come here before you can even see her or anything 'cause they got to ask you some questions." And it was dragging on and dragging on. I told that security guard, "He's got five more minutes to get a cop here 'cause him and his buddy can't stop me from going in that room. I guarantee you won't [inaudible 02:19:15]." All right. So at some point, did Detective Leatherwood come and talk to you at the hospital? Okay. All right. And you talked to Detective Leatherwood while you were at the hospital? Let me take you back to the night of November 12th. You said previously that at the house that night, inside your house- ... I know of. Like I said, I was in bed and I don't think David was inside the house. I think he was outside with his friends. And where do they live? Do they live outside, inside? Or ... In and ... Both, in and out. I mean, they leave in in the night and we let them out the first thing in the morning when I go to work so they can use the restroom and everything. And Lisa's there in the daytime, so then I let them back in the house so they don't try to follow me down the road. All right. Did you see anybody inside your house the night of the 12th going into the early morning hours of the 13th? Okay. Did you see David come back into the house or hear David come back to the house as Lisa described? Outside of waking up around the time that Savannah comes into your room, did you wake up between the time you went to bed at 8:00 or 9:00 in the morning to the time that Savannah comes into your room? Did you wake up any other- Just to go take a pee. I used the restroom and then I was coming back laying down and that's when she came into the restroom and told me that. All right. So from the time 8:00 or nine o'clock on the 12th to the time you got up to the restroom- Did you go into the living room with the girls at all between the time you go to bed at 8:00 or 9:00 to the time you go to the restroom? No, sir. I usually go in there and check on them, but for some morning I didn't. I looked in the room, you know, I looked through the door 'cause of the what you call it right there, I seen Savannah standing up and I seen Paitin laying down. I thought she was asleep, so I went on and laid back down to bed. All right. So you didn't go in there into the living room with the girls between the time you went to bed, 8:00 or 9:00 that night to the time you woke up to go to the bathroom? No, sir. I just peeked then I'm on through the door while I was going back to the bathroom. And then as you're getting in the bed, Savannah comes in and says... I can't tell you. It might have been five, might have been 10, you know what I mean? But somewhere around there. All right. She comes in, you send her out, or you tell her to go back to bed? All right. At some point after Savannah tells you that something was funny with Paitin, does Lisa wake up? When it got about time for the alarm to come up, you know what I mean? She woke up right before the alarm come on to go make my coffee. Okay. And you heard that Lisa testified just now that she woke up when you went to go to the bathroom. Did you hear that? Yes. She usually now ... That's something if I get out of bed, she will pop her eyes out. I don't know what it is. She knows when her husband gets up out of that bed. At some point you're told by medical personnel or by Pender County Sheriff's Office what happened to Paitin, correct? Yeah. The guy from Pender County came in there and told me I had a very, very sick granddaughter, that they got her under ... Her seizures under control and that she's very sick and she's going to have to go to New Hanover. Yes, sir. Like I said, we had Savannah since she was 10 days old. I spoiled my grand babies. Yes, sir. Just briefly. Mr. Hunt, you and Savannah share the same birthday, don't you? You had an opportunity to see David with both of the girls, hadn't you? How would you describe his relationship with both of the girls? He loves his niece. He spoiled him just as much as I did. I just popped in my head. That was when he was little. He reminded me of a Boo Boo and that's just what it came ever since he was about 19-months-old, two-years-old. It's stuck, and everybody says when something happens, they say, "Well, it's the boo-boo. He's spoiled. He's the baby. It's the boo-boo." Which was it? She wake you up or did you wake up on your own? Like I said, I just went and used the bathroom. I was laying back down. I hadn't quite fallen asleep yet when she came in there. She said that, "Paitin was in there." I want to say, "She was acting silly." I thought they was just in there playing, so I told her to go back to sleep and let her sister go back to sleep, 'cause Savannah went to sleep a lot earlier than her sister did that night 'cause she got in trouble for walking Savannah around with a dog leash on her neck. To Paitin, yes, sir. She had a dog leash around her neck. And so when you told Savannah to go back into the living room and go back to sleep, did she do what you told her? Did she go back in there? Yes, sir. My wife takes care of us. If I got to work, she makes sure I'm taken care of. And so you knew she got up and walked out of the bedroom? She was holding Savannah and saying, "Something ain't right, baby. Something ain't right. She's having a seizure." Now, were you aware that Savannah had been sick the day before? Yes, sir. Matter of fact, I think Friday, my wife took her to a doctor's or something or some emergency room or something, but she had a doctor appointment the next day, that Monday. And who would normally take her to the doctor? Lisa? And so when you heard Lisa scream, you just jumped out of bed? Yeah, 'cause it was the most banshee-ist ... I knew something was wrong from that scream. So you had not gotten up and started to get dressed, you jumped out of bed? And then when you came into the living room, was David already there? And the clothes that we saw him wearing in the video at the hospital? And so, did you stay in the room or did you go back to the bedroom? I went back to the bedroom and got changed, put some clothes on so we can go to the emergency room. Where was Paitin when you went back to the bedroom? I don't know. I can't tell you if Lisa was holding her or by then Boo Boo was holding her. So there came a point when you came out and you were dressed, y'all made a decision to go- Yes, sir. When that emergency call didn't come in, we weren't going to wait another ... 'Cause we didn't know how long it would be. When he got into the car, did he continue to hold her? I remember him, like, at one time I told him I kept my eye on the road, but I remember looking over here and giving him mouth-to-mouth. He was giving her mouth-to-mouth 'cause that's when she defecated and he said, "Daddy, let's go." And that's when I hit 160. So you were aware that she had lost control of her bowel? When you got to the hospital, were David's clothes wet or dry? They was wet to where she lost control of her body fluids. And so you dropped David ... You pulled into the ambulance bay, David gets out and he bangs on the door? Yes, sir. And I take my car and I drive around to the parking lot and I come through the front door. So David is the one who rushes her into the emergency room? No, sir. She was back in one of those rooms in the back. I think he was in the room back there. When I got back there, I think he was in the room and I was in the room and they kicked us both out the room saying, "You know what I mean? There ain't enough room to get to work on her." And so did you stay in the lobby or did you go outside? What'd you do? I think I stayed in the lobby for a minute and then I went outside and smoked me a cigarette, waited for Lisa to get there, and I think we came, me and Lisa and them came back in together. Did you ask David if he knew what was going on with her? No, sir. I don't think so. Oh, we had a doctor come ... After Lisa came in there, we had a doctor come out there and that's when he told us that we had a very sick girl, but they got the seizures under control, but she was going to have to go to New Hanover. Greater care, which I didn't think it must have been that bad since it took two and a half hours for the ambulance to get there, 'cause when I went to take Boo Boo home so he could change his clothes, they were sitting right there at Shell's getting them some food and a cup of coffee. And when I come back, they were still sitting at Shell's. And so you took David home, he changed his clothes. Did y'all leave to go back to the hospital together? Yes or no, was there any conversation between you and David while you were going back to the hospital? And at some point, did anyone at New Hanover come out and speak to you, Lisa, and David about Paitin's condition? They wouldn't let us have nothing to do with her in New Hanover. We couldn't go nowhere around her. Only as far as we could get was in the parking lot. Yes, sir. He put us in the interview room, and that's when I told him, I said, "When she wakes up, she can tell you what in the world is going on." I think she was in there. I think she's the first one they took back there. Yeah. We were all emotions. I was in the parking lot begging God to take my life. I've been here 50-some years. The stuff I've done, I don't deserve to live, you know. And so when you returned home from New Hanover, was David at the house? Eventually, did David leave with Jamie or did he remain there at home? And to your knowledge, did he spend the night there that night or did he go to- Did David spend the night, Monday, at home with you and Lisa, or did he go somewhere else? Okay. All right. Thank you. I don't have any other questions at this time. Redirect, just briefly. You just said that you've done stuff you've done, you don't deserve to live. What'd you do? Yeah, I was mean when I was young. I used to fight all the time. All right, sir, you're still subject to the obligation of your subpoena, so that means if they call you again to testify, you have to come back and testify. Move this chair. Please come this way. Watch your step, sir. Mm-hmm. [inaudible 02:36:12] exit the [inaudible 02:36:13]. All right. Counsel can approach. All right, members of the jury, there's a bit of a sickness going around. So what we're going to do is we're going to break for the day, allow you an extra little bit of time for the weekend. So go ahead and close up your notebooks. Go ahead and take off your red badges, pin them to your notebooks. Now, as you go home for the weekend, remind you again, do not discuss this case amongst yourselves and do not discuss this case with anybody else. There may be more people that you interact with this weekend than you interacted with during this week. Those people are also going to be curious, and you are also going to have to explain to them that you are forbidden from speaking with them about this case. You are also forbidden from having any contact with any of the parties, attorneys, or witnesses. (02:38:02)You cannot conduct any independent investigation or inquiry. If you happen to go by any of the locations that were mentioned, you may pass by them, but you are not allowed to stop. Obviously, if there are any emergencies that require you to go to the hospital, you may do so, but not to conduct any independent investigation. You're not to post online on any social media sites regarding your experience as a juror or any of the evidence you've seen or heard. You're also not allowed to have anybody discuss this case in your presence. So you are excused. We will reconvene again Monday morning at 9:30. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honor. Make sure your notebooks are closed once again and your juror badge is attached the same way as those in your chairs and ready front row, then back this way, please. Quiet in the courtroom, please. Ma'am, quiet in the courtroom. Thank you, sir. Let the record reflect that the jury has exited the courtroom. We had, there were a number of bench conferences. First was Mr. Britt's concern regarding our poor clerk. He definitely was not feeling very well. We had another one just before the jury broke that I indicated that we were just going to break for the remainder of the day, given the sickness that might be going around. The bailiff with the jurors came up and approached me. He said a juror had asked him about asking the bailiff questions regarding the trial. I'm going to have him come back in and explain that on the record just so that we all know exactly what was asked. As far as this session is concerned, it is the Friday after the Monday in which this trial calendar had begun. (02:40:25)The session not having concluded during the pendency of this week. Court retains jurisdiction regarding this case and any other matters on the trial calendar, and we will continue the matter through next week or until its conclusion. And I'll enter an order extending the session. Is there anything that we need to discuss on behalf of the state while we're waiting for the bailiff to come back in? All right. If you want to just let him know that as soon as he's ready to come back in the courtroom. Thank you. (02:41:28)Mr. Bailiff, you indicated that a juror had asked you a question. Can you explain that question again? Yes. Juror number eight was asking in reference to the proceedings outside of the courtroom setting, would he be able to ask me any questions? And then I immediately informed you of same, Your Honor. All right. Thank you. Anything you wish to say regarding that, Mr. Britt? All right. Then we will go ahead and be in recess until Monday morning at 9:30. If the parties here can remain and if we can go off audio and the video. Anybody- Luckily for you, we deliver. title: Beyond Fest 2026 Review: V/H/S/MIXTAPE Keeps The Franchise Rocking - Daily Dead
content: Some horror franchises mature; V/H/S seems to be growing more rebellious with each entry. V/H/S/Mixtape continues Shudder’s stellar anthology run behind producer Josh Goldbloom, tuning into audio horror frequencies. Most segments theme around music: an 80s-era metal video; armageddon compositions; songs made by the dead. It’s a madcap moshpit of filmmaking talent, from Wu-Tang leaders to New French Extremity stalwarts to alien Scumdogs, bound together with a punk-as-fuck attitude. Not to say every inclusion is a winner; most are a riot of rhythmic massacres and gnarly practical effects—another successful grab-bag of unpredictable shorts, infected butt warts and all. The film wastes no time subjecting audiences to its repulsive behaviors by introducing notorious Virginia metal gods GWAR as its wraparound hosts. V/H/S/Mixtape doesn’t roll for more than two minutes before slime-green space jizz coats hot dogs, honoring GWAR’s shock-rock insanity. The whole gang is there—Blöthar the Berserker, Beefcake the Mighty, Balsac the Jaws of Death—bringing their bloodthirsty bonehead sense of humor. It’s one of my favorite wraparounds, but with the disclaimer that I’m a massive GWAR fan who's been covered in their concert juices before. The band is given a blank canvas, which means lots of stammering scatological improv, GWAR tracks laid under grotesque mutilation sequences, or necrophiliac fitness workouts—surely not everyone’s cup of tea. But V/H/S/Mixtape is smart about its chapter arrangement, which keeps momentum churning as smoothly as possible. It’s bumpy in the middle, with lulls of inflated storytelling and an entire segment that feels out of place. Still, the team nails what matters most: the intro and the outro. Renee Zhan’s “Dance, Dance, Dance, Dance” welcomes us into Jim Henson’s workshop if it went all Five Nights at Freddy’s, while RZA’s “Death Tone” brings us home with a serial-killer riff on Dexter meets American Psycho, set in the music industry. The bookends are the strongest, reeling us in and sending us home gobsmacked by the artistic impressiveness of turning corpses into a chart-topping hit. Variety is both a tool and a struggle for V/H/S/Mixtape, but way less the latter. “Dance, Dance, Dance, Dance” (written by Zoe Cooper) sends Barbara Crampton and others into the adorable felt world of a canceled children’s program, only for the puppets to fight back as the Henson warehouse comes entirely to life. It’s unlike David Moreau’s “Heartbeat,” about idiot vloggers who lock themselves inside a defunct sound-deprivation chamber, or Ernest Dickerson’s “The Music of Mr. Sze.” Filmmakers operate on their own exciting wavelengths, with Flying Lotus and Tobias Forge (Ghost) adding bite-sized music videos to the menu. From the Lovecraftian to the technological, the stop-motion-sorta animated to the orchestral, each segment guards unique ideas and taps into a host of fears. That said, V/H/S/Mixtape exhibits your usual anthology highs and lows. Where Forge’s “Premature Burial” resurrects his death metal band Repugnant for a vengeful music video that fits the vibe, Flying Lotus’ “Another Cabin” feels odd as an animated music video, even outside the loose constraint of V/H/S entries being filmed in found-footage style. Dickerson’s story of a mysterious violinist and the evils tethered to his music could use a first-half trim before a deliriously awesome payoff brimming with monstrous visuals. Despite their serviceable work as the exploitation hounds holding everything together, even GWAR could have used some wrangling, as they chomp on video cassettes and act like clueless warrior buffoons trying to make sense of their instructions (and humanity). As for gore, V/H/S/Mixtape reinforces the argument that V/H/S has become a dependable source of exquisite violence. Credit Los Angeles-based SFX company Little Shop of Gore (Ryan & Salina Ward), who showcase their love of prosthetics, cosmetics, and other do-it-yourself methods for turning butchered bodies into magnificent highlights. “Dance, Dance, Dance, Dance” features one of my favorite killings of the year, not just because it’s at the hands of Lamb Chop wannabes singing their happy little ditty as they [redacted] with a [redacted]. “Death Tone” is a smorgasbord of gruesome musician-themed murderers, carried out by the top-performing Neela Jolene, who swings an axe and waves her chainsaw with appealing villainy. The Wards are quickly making a name for themselves as go-to indie horror SFX specialists, not to mention the other segments that feature their mind-blowing work (literally), plus other hired SFX artists, who punt decapitated heads and chew into bleeding flesh. V/H/S/Mixtape is a robust collection of mix-and-match horrors that feel like flipping through channels on a cursed television set. We’re nine films in, and the V/H/S franchise only inspires more optimism—that alone is a miracle. Goldbloom’s behind-the-scenes work curating rosters, cultivating ideas, and stitching it all together has made V/H/S Shudder’s Halloween tradition, which is well deserved. V/H/S/Mixtape is another example of why the series has amassed its fanbase, defying the odds with another slaughter-happy, sloppy-silly, you-can’t-stop-us entry tailor-made to kickstart your October movie marathons with an amp-bursting bang. Matt Donato is a Los Angeles-based film critic currently published on SlashFilm, Fangoria, Bloody Disgusting, and anywhere else he’s allowed to spread the gospel of Demon Wind. He is also a member of the Critics Choice Association. Definitely don’t feed him after midnight. title: Visa (V) Is Considered a Good Investment by Brokers: Is That True? - Yahoo Finance UK
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though? Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Visa (V). Visa currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.24, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 41 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.24 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy. Of the 41 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 34 are Strong Buy and four are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 82.9% and 9.8% of all recommendations. Check price target & stock forecast for Visa here>>> While the ABR calls for buying Visa, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential. Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations. In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement. Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision. In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures. Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5. It has been and continues to be the case that analysts employed by brokerage firms are overly optimistic with their recommendations. Because of their employers' vested interests, these analysts issue more favorable ratings than their research would support, misguiding investors far more often than helping them. In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research. Furthermore, the different grades of the Zacks Rank are applied proportionately across all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide earnings estimates for the current year. In other words, at all times, this tool maintains a balance among the five ranks it assigns. There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices. In terms of earnings estimate revisions for Visa, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 0% over the past month to $13.22. Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Visa. title: CLÁSICO PREVIEW | Barcelona v Real Madrid - FC Barcelona Website
content: It's time for another Barça Femení Clásico at the Spotify Camp Nou (kick-off 7:00pm CEST). The league leaders are taking on their nearest rivals in a match that is always charged with plenty of emotion both on and off the pitch. The blaugranes come into it with an unblemished record of seven wins from seven so far this season – five in the domestic league and two in the Champions League. The all-whites have 13 points in the domestic league and two draws in Europe. Coach Pere Romeu gave his thoughts on the game in the pre-match press conference on Saturday. “​​The last game against Roma was one of the greatest games I have managed as a coach. It wasn't just a resounding victory, we played really well. This was really significant given what we had to deal with in September. We are also really developing as a team and I think that's worth mentioning. It will be a different and exciting Clásico, as they all are, and we will have to be at our best to come through the game”. The blaugrana coach also assessed their opponent's start to the season and style of play. “It's a different Real Madrid to last season. The team were a lot more direct last season, they played with more forwards, and this season they are playing with a midfield set up that is keeping the ball more, controlling possession. This means their attacking sequences are a bit longer than last season. It's a Real Madrid with new components and a slightly different style”. And he went on to discuss what might prove key in the match: “We have to keep the ball a lot, push hard after we lose it and try to limit the number of Real Madrid attacking transitions. We know they have other strengths, but one is fast play, counterattacks. If we manage that aspect properly, I'm sure we can come through in this game. This means we have to play a similar match to what we did in Rome, a lot of possession, hardly lose the ball, set the pace of the game. We have to avoid a basketball-type match, especially against a side like Real Madrid”. Pere Romeu has called up 20 players for the match: Gemma, Paredes, Van Asten, Sydney, Kerolin, Marta, Pina, Graham, Patri, Cata Coll, Aitana, C. Serrajordi, Pajor, Carla Julià, Brugts, Aïcha, Martina, McCamey, Rosalía and Mayssa. Today marks exactly six years since the first women's Clásico was played at the Valdebebas stadium. Barça ran out 0-4 winners, with Patri Guijarro scoring the first goal. Barça have managed to win 24 out of 25 of the games between both sides, which included the record setting match on 22 April 2022, when 91,648 were in attendance at the Spotify Camp Nou.

title: France predicted XI v Belgium: Liverpool duo Jérémy Jacquet and Bradley Barcola to start - Yahoo Sports
content: France host Belgium tonight at Saint-Denis' Stade de France for Matchday 4 of the 2026-2027 UEFA Nations League. It will be the fourth and final game for Les Bleus in this extended international break. Zinédine Zidane's France are top of their group with seven points out of a possible nine. Les Bleus have been halted on Friday by Roberto Mancini's Italy (1-1). For tonight's encounter against Mark van Bommel's Belgium, Zidane won't rely on Dayot Upamecano, who has been sent off against the Italians. The Bayern Munich centre-back has been allowed to return to Germany. In his absence, Liverpool sensation Jérémy Jacquet will play a third straight game. The 21-year-old is expected to form an all-Premier League defense with Chelsea's Maxence Lacroix, L'Equipe reports. Barcelona right-back Jules Koundé, who was benched for France's last two games, will regain his place. On the other defensive flank, Adrien Truffert retains his spot after a convincing left-back shift against the Azzurri. Zidane is expected to tweak his team as Manu Koné and Eduardo Camavinga are poised to start in a three-man midfield with Manchester City's Rayan Cherki. Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé is expected to be dropped after poor performances at the tip of France's attack. Rennes' Estéban Lepaul will be given another go as France's centre-forward. Liverpool's Bradley Barcola and Bayern Munich's Michael Olise are poised to be deployed as wingers. Mike Maignan; Adrien Truffert, Maxence Lacroix, Jérémy Jacquet, Jules Koundé; Eduardo Camavinga, Manu Koné, Rayan Cherki; Bradley Barcola, Estéban Lepaul, Michael Olise. (L'Éq)

title: Q3 Power donation gives CC-V athletics an upgrade - Colorado Springs Gazette
content:
For student-athletes at Cripple Creek-Victor High School, some new gear is on the way — and some of it has already been ordered. A $35,000 donation from Q3 Power is giving the school’s athletic department a boost, helping pay for new uniforms, updated equipment and other athletic department needs. For Luke Harrison, Cripple Creek-Victor’s head girls basketball coach, the timing couldn’t be much better. “We just ordered new uniforms this morning,” Harrison said. “The kids are going to get new stuff and it’s a really big change from the way it has been, I think, as far as the funding goes.” Harrison has coached at Cripple Creek for four years and is heading into his third year as a head coach. During that time, he said he hasn’t seen anything close to a donation this size. “This is easily, easily the biggest single donation that we’ve gotten in that time and I’m sure it’s the biggest in much longer than that,” he said. The money isn’t just for basketball; the donation will benefit the athletic department as a whole. Uniforms were first on the shopping list because they can take about two months to arrive. With basketball season approaching, Harrison said they needed to move quickly. Volleyball is already well into its season, so those players are expected to receive new uniforms for next season. Some programs, including track and field and cross country, may not need new uniforms because theirs were replaced more recently. The remaining money is still being discussed, Harrison said, but it could go toward equipment such as basketballs and other athletic department needs. Q3 Power CEO Rod Kagy said the company wanted its support to reach students in the community. “We want to be a company that doesn’t just operate in this community but is part of it,” Kagy said. “These students work hard and represent this community well. When we learned there was a need, we wanted to help.” At a small school like Cripple Creek-Victor, a donation can stretch a long way. Uniforms wear out. Equipment needs replacing. And unlike a large school with dozens of athletes trying out for a team, Harrison’s girls basketball squad may have just seven or eight players this season. That small roster comes with challenges, but Harrison sees an upside. “It also means that I get to know everybody really well and there’s a good team atmosphere,” he said. Harrison’s own road to coaching girls basketball wasn’t exactly mapped out. He attended Colorado Springs Christian School, where he played football and a year of basketball. He later coached there for about five years and also played semi-professional football. After moving to the area in 2017, he stepped away from coaching for a couple of years. Eventually, though, the itch came back. So Harrison drove up to Cripple Creek and asked what the school needed help with. A former football coach, Harrison took the first head coaching opening available — girls basketball. “I’m coaching girls basketball, I just had my third daughter,” Harrison joked. “There’s just girls everywhere.” Now he is preparing for another season, this time with some new uniforms and fewer worries about how the athletic department will pay for what its students need. Earlier this year, Harrison said, coaches were already discussing how they were going to fund some of those expenses. “They basically came through and solved that problem,” Harrison said. For the athletes, the result will soon be easy to spot. New uniforms. New equipment. And, for a small-town athletic department accustomed to making things stretch, a little more breathing room. title: MSDF deploys V-BAT uncrewed surveillance aircraft - The Japan Times
content:
The Maritime Self-Defense Force has introduced the V-BAT uncrewed reconnaissance aircraft as part of a broader effort to strengthen surveillance capabilities while easing personnel requirements. The MSDF operates six V-BATs developed by U.S. defense technology company Shield AI, according to officials. The aircraft can autonomously patrol predetermined routes, collecting surveillance footage and transmitting it to a command vessel in real time. Measuring 2.9 meters long and 3.8 meters across, the V-BAT is equipped with an infrared camera in its nose and can remain continuously airborne for up to about 12 hours. A key advantage is its high operational flexibility. The aircraft can be folded and stored aboard a destroyer when not in use, then assembled by two crew members in about 10 minutes. Its ability to take off and land vertically allows it to operate from a destroyer’s deck without a runway. The deployment reflects the Defense Ministry’s push to expand the use of uncrewed systems, a central element of the “new ways of warfare” outlined in Japan’s 2026 defense white paper. The ministry is accelerating the introduction of various types of uncrewed aircraft in hopes of securing what it calls an “asymmetric advantage” over potential adversaries through superior cost efficiency and technological capabilities. The V-BAT has been deployed in the war in Ukraine. According to Shield AI’s website and other sources, Ukrainian forces had flown 130 or more sorties with the aircraft as of April 2025. The system has also been adopted by countries including Canada and India. The MSDF allocated about ¥4 billion ($25.3 million) in its fiscal 2025 budget for the acquisition of six V-BATs. In August 2026, it began operational training with the aircraft at its Ominato Air Base in Aomori Prefecture. Each V-BAT costs about ¥600 million, far less than the price tag of about ¥11 billion for the SH-60L, the MSDF’s newest patrol helicopter. “Drones allow us to conduct missions at a lower cost than helicopters. They also help ease burdens on personnel,” an MSDF member said. Efforts to introduce drones extend beyond the MSDF. In April 2026, the Ground Self-Defense Force established two dedicated units: the Unmanned Defense Capability Promotion Office, responsible for research and development involving uncrewed aerial vehicles and other equipment; and the Unmanned Systems Office, which oversees the procurement and maintenance of such systems. In its fiscal 2026 budget, the Defense Ministry earmarked about ¥100 billion to establish the Synchronized, Hybrid, Integrated and Enhanced Littoral Defense, or SHIELD, system by fiscal 2027. The multilayered coastal defense network will employ not only uncrewed aircraft but also uncrewed surface and underwater vessels. The use of uncrewed systems has expanded worldwide since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. The Defense Ministry’s goals of reducing personnel requirements and securing an asymmetric advantage reflect lessons drawn from this trend. Specifically, the ministry plans to combine uncrewed systems with artificial intelligence to enhance their operational capabilities. By forcing adversaries to deploy large numbers of costly crewed platforms and other assets in response, Japan aims to impose substantial operational costs on them and gain an advantage through such “asymmetric warfare.” One challenge is how to respond when an aircraft encounters problems in flight. On Sept. 15, a Global Hawk — a large uncrewed aircraft operated by the Air Self-Defense Force — crashed off the coast of Tottori Prefecture. The aircraft is designed to land autonomously at a designated location in an emergency, but that function apparently failed to operate properly. “This accident will serve as an important lesson,” a senior ministry official said. “Nevertheless, the shift toward uncrewed aircraft is likely to continue.” In a time of both misinformation and too much information, quality journalism is more crucial than ever.By subscribing, you can help us get the story right. title: Supreme Court set to hear Suncor v. Boulder climate lawsuit arguments - The Center Square
content: The U.S. Supreme Court in Washington, D.C. Photo: massmatt / Flickr / CC BY 2.0 / Cropped from Original (The Center Square) – The U.S. Supreme Court is set to hear oral arguments Monday in Suncor Energy v. Boulder County. Supporters of Suncor and ExxonMobil argue there will be nationwide consequences as a result of this and dozens of other similar cases while some expressed confidence that the court will not allow one county to decide the energy policy of the nation. CEO of the American Energy Institute Jason Isaac told The Center Square that “the Supreme Court will hear the most consequential energy case of the term, and it isn't really about Suncor or ExxonMobil. “It's about whether a single county's jury can dictate energy policy for the entire country, a power the Constitution gives to Congress, not a courtroom in Boulder,” Isaac said. “The Justice Department itself has now told the Court as much, warning that one city cannot use its own state's law to set the rules for energy production nationwide,” Isaac said. “American Energy is confident the Court will side with the Constitution over courtroom lawfare, and with it, every American who fills a gas tank or pays a power bill,” Isaac said. Ongoing for years, Suncor Energy v. Boulder is essentially a lawsuit where Colorado’s Boulder County is attempting to make energy companies pay for the damages caused by climate change The Center Square reported it is “a case challenging whether state and local governments can utilize tort laws to seek billions in damages against energy companies over alleged contributions to climate change.” The Supreme Court agreed to hear the case in February 2026, with oral arguments set for Monday, Oct. 5. In August, 28 amicus briefs were filed in support of Boulder County, with a watchdog warning many of the briefs had connections to left-wing organizations and dark money. The briefs argue that the Supreme Court should allow the lawsuit brought by Boulder County go to trial. At a panel discussion hosted by the conservative Civitas Institute, University of Georgia law professor Hillel Levin said that federal law doesn't preclude state and local laws in cases such as this and it should go to trial. But president of the Judicial Crisis Network (JCN) Carrie Severino told The Center Square that Suncor v. Boulder “is a last resort for climate activists, who are attempting to hold energy companies accountable for past and future harm they say stems from global climate change.” “The case is part of a broader push by the left to weaponize the court and enact extreme environmental policies through lawfare, rather than through support from voters and lawmakers,” Severino said. Severino warned that “if Boulder succeeds, the floodgates could be open for states like Colorado and California to set national climate policy and regulate a number of industries in other states.” Executive director of consumer advocacy group Alliance for Consumers O.H. Skinner likewise told The Center Square that the lawsuit in question is a case of lawfare, or creating policies through the courtroom rather than the traditional legislative process. “Having lost at the ballot box, climate activists have turned to the courts to force through extreme policies that voters have rejected repeatedly,” Skinner said. “The Supreme Court’s ruling in Suncor will determine how far outside their borders a county or state may project their regulatory powers, and whether the nation’s energy policy is to be set by Congress or progressive activists in Boulder, Colorado,” Skinner said. As a point of interest, Severino told The Center Square how a “member of Boulder’s legal team admitted that their strategy is a bid to impose a ‘carbon tax’ that could bankrupt the energy industry and ultimately harm the American consumer.” “Beyond that, the sweeping claims at issue in Suncor could open the floodgates for similar lawfare-based litigation involving cars, firearms, and other sectors that are a huge part of everyday life,” Severino said. title: NFL today: How to watch Chiefs v Raiders, TV channels & live stream Sunday 4 October - The Guardian
content: How will the Chiefs and Raiders fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options Disorienting as it may sound given the past 12 years of Chiefs-Raiders matchups, their game Sunday in Las Vegas is one of the blockbusters of the young NFL season. Kansas City have used Las Vegas (and before that, Oakland) as a doormat since the 2015 season, when Patrick Mahomes was a sophomore at Texas Tech. The Chiefs took both games from the Raiders that year and began a run of 18 wins in the teams’ last 22 contests, an unusual run of AFC West dominance in a league that adores parity. The Chiefs are favored again this week, but by less than a touchdown. The Silver and Black come in sporting a matching 3-0 record with their Missourian visitors. Kirk Cousins has found the fountain of youth at 38, keeping No 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza in an understudy’s role for at least a while longer. The 38-year-old has averaged at least 7.5 yards per pass attempt in each of the team’s three wins, two of which came on the road. The Raiders have benefited from a light opening schedule, taking advantage of games against the moribund Dolphins and Saints. Now comes a stiff test in the desert. United Kingdom: Watch on Sky Sports NFL or Sky Sports Football, or stream with NOW. Just how back is Patrick Mahomes? The answer might be “extremely.” The franchise QB was having the worst season of his career last year even before it ended a few weeks early because of a torn ACL. But now, Mahomes looks both accurate and unusually spry, like a man who’s gained mobility from chasing a bunch of little kids around his house. He is also benefiting massively from the arrival of Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker at running back. Walker is the league’s leading rusher, with 360 yards in his first three games with K.C. It’s not just volume, either; his 5.8 yards per touch are a career best. Cousins is getting the publicity, but the Raiders’ greatest strength to date is one that should come in extra handy against Mahomes: their sublime pass rush. Only one club, the Vikings, have generated more pressures than Vegas, according to Pro Football Reference. The biggest chunk of those (13) have come from the freakishly good Maxx Crosby, who only remains with the team because the Ravens backed out of a trade the teams had agreed to in March. It’s a team effort, though: Crosby only has two of the Raiders’ 10 sacks to date, a figure that places them tied for fourth. Mahomes will be minding his blind side.

title: Poetry Moment: 'to be the bird' by nicole v basta - WPSU
content: This is Poetry Moment on WPSU – a weekly program featuring the work of contemporary Pennsylvania poets. Your host is poet and author Marjorie Maddox, a 2023 Monson Arts Fellow, author of more than 20 books, and Professor Emerita of English and Creative Writing at the Lock Haven campus of Commonwealth University. Welcome to Poetry Moment. I’m Marjorie MaddoxWho hasn't, at some point, yearned to be a bird? In today's poem, "to be the bird," nicole v basta considers the storks of Poland, where, before moving to Pennsylvania, her ancestors lived, eventually working in the coal mines and garment factories of Wilkes-Barre. nicole v basta (who does not use capital letters in her name) is a 2026 Academy of American Poets Laureate Fellow. Her poems have appeared in Ploughshares, Blackbird, Third Coast, North American Review, and elsewhere. Her second chapbook, "the next field over" (2022), was published by Tolsun Books. nicole is also a community educator, arts events producer, and visual artist. Her work has been supported by grants and residencies, including Art Farm Nebraska, Monson Arts, and The Saltonstall Foundation. Currently, she is Poet Laureate of Tompkins County/Ithaca, New York. I'm told that, in Poland, storks migrate large distances to winter in Africa. After that long absence, their return is met with great anticipation. According to one source, "the sight of a stork circling overhead or tending to its massive nest is more than just a glimpse of nature; it’s a symbol of rebirth, good fortune, and deep cultural connection."... [S]torks restoring their nests. . . is a potent symbol [both] of renewal" and warmer days ("Storks: Poland's Beloved Harbingers of Spring"). In her poem, "to be the bird," nicole v basta also welcomes this majestic bird, embracing its "kind of solitude" as a gift. on the roof, a stork nests and dreams of a past lifewading in the shallow water of another continent beneath the roof, a woman goes on with her luckkneels to the narrow altar in the home she made of her body alone— suppose the silence after a quest-ion begins a new day, the quiet bouncing off the brims of hats— words like spar and spark, shoulder, the secondstar, limp in the air like lazy ghosts and suppose the answers arrive as the birds, not as the birthsthey've come to represent in the west, no, we're in the old country now and it is a gift, that kind of solitudethe one when there is no echo of yourself who breathes and what i am saying is— i may only wantto be the bird Originally published in Colorado Review Volume 50, Number 1, Spring 2023 Listen for Poetry Moment with Marjorie Maddox, Mondays during Morning Edition and All Things Considered on WPSU. title: Michigan v Minnesota recap, results: Gophers beat Wolverines at home for the first time since 1977 - Yahoo Sports
content: The Little Brown Jug is staying in Minneapolis after Minnesota beat Michigan at home for the first time in nearly 50 years. The Golden Gophers (4-1) held the Wolverines (3-2) scoreless in the second half of a 20-14 victory Saturday. It's Minnesota's first home victory over Michigan since 1977, an 18-game streak that ended with Gophers fans storming the field. "This team's heart, their how, their spirit," Minnesota coach PJ Fleck said. "Our community and state, they never stop believing in anything. This team is resilient. There's pandemonium in Minneapolis right now." Michigan held a 14-7 lead at halftime but had the ball for only 47 seconds in the third quarter because of three consecutive turnovers, the first on a muffed punt by Andrew Marsh and then an interceptions by quarterback Bryce Underwood. Michigan started the fourth quarter on another interception by Underwood, who completed 10 of 21 passes for 101 yards and a QB rating of 69. Minnesota took the lead for good on a 3-yard TD reception by Darius Taylor from Drake Lindsey, who completed 17 of 25 passes for 136 yards. Minnesota's most recent win in the series that awards The Little Brown Jug was 12 years ago in Ann Arbor. "Besides my marriage, my kids being born, this might be the best day in my life," Fleck said.
